patients.text: I have severe impostor syndrome at work, despite being employee of the month for six consecutive years.
Whenever someone calls me on the phone without texting first, my fight-or-flight response activates immediately.
I rehearse ordering coffee three times in my head and still say 'You too!' when the barista says 'Enjoy your drink'.
I cannot start studying or working until my room is spotless, my laundry is done, and it is suddenly 3:00 AM.
I keep adding $400 worth of luxury items to my online shopping cart just to feel a spark of joy, then close the tab.
I get into heated, emotionally draining imaginary arguments in the shower and end up furious with people who did nothing.
I refuse to watch an acclaimed 2-hour movie because 'I don't have time', then watch 4 hours of raccoon videos.
I apologize profusely when someone else accidentally bumps into ME in the supermarket.
I checked WebMD for an itchy elbow and am now 98% convinced I have a rare 17th-century pirate plague.
I maintain a private mental tier list of my friends based strictly on how quickly they react to my memes.
I hear the Microsoft Teams chime on a Sunday evening and my heart rate jumps to 180 BPM.
I set 12 alarms in 4-minute intervals, wake up before the first one, and still end up 20 minutes late.
I haven't opened my physical postal mail in five months because bad news legally cannot hurt me if it remains sealed.
I pretend to be deeply engaged with my smartphone while walking past a coworker in the corridor to avoid eye contact.
I sent a 3-minute voice message, immediately re-listened to it twice to evaluate my cadence, and cringed into the abyss.
I bought an expensive ergonomic chair, a standing desk, and 4 houseplants, but I still work slouched like a boiled shrimp on the sofa.
I can't go to sleep unless my closet door is 100% shut, otherwise the demon has a tactical line of sight.
I feel an intense moral obligation to wave politely at cars that stop at pedestrian crossings, even though they are legally required to.
I bought a 900-page classic novel to look cultured in coffee shops, but I've been stuck on chapter 2 for eighteen months.
I have 47 browser tabs open across three windows because 'I might need that recipe for homemade sourdough in 2028'.
I feel guilty calling in sick when I am literally shaking with a 102°F fever and unable to see straight.
I have an overwhelming urge to clean the house only when I have a high-stakes deadline due in 45 minutes.
Whenever an email begins with 'Per my previous email', I spend the next hour drafting revenge plots in my head.
I stare into my fully stocked refrigerator for 10 minutes, sigh loudly, and decide there is nothing to eat.
I get anxious when Spotify Wrapped drops because I fear my music taste will expose my spiritual bankruptcy.
I left a WhatsApp group without explanation because someone used the wrong 'their', and now I feel like an international fugitive.
I nodded along to a conversation for 20 minutes without hearing a single word because I was wondering if pigeons have feelings.
I purchased gym clothes, a gym shaker, and pre-workout powder, but my primary workout is carrying groceries up the stairs.
I obsessively track package deliveries every 12 minutes as if my psychic gaze will make the courier drive faster.
I spent three hours customizing my avatar in an RPG, started the game, and immediately stopped playing forever.
I feel personally attacked when a YouTube video has an unskippable 15-second ad about life insurance.
I accidentally made eye contact with my Uber driver in the rearview mirror and had to pretend to look at a cloud for 15 miles.
I refuse to use the big light in the living room because ambient lighting is the only thing keeping my sanity together.
I have drafted 15 polite ways to cancel social plans that I voluntarily made yesterday with immense enthusiasm.
I get deeply offended when someone tells me I look tired, even when I have had 3 hours of sleep and look like a goblin.
I keep buying notebooks because they smell like potential, yet I refuse to write in them because my handwriting will ruin them.
I walked into a room, forgot why I entered, spun around in a circle, and walked back out pretending I had a plan.
I panic when a retail worker approaches and asks 'Can I help you find anything?' and reply 'Just looking!' while clutching a lawnmower.
I hold onto clothing from eight years ago in case style trends cycle back to neon skinny jeans.
I wrote a to-do list consisting only of tasks I already completed just so I could experience the rush of crossing them off.

therapies.text: Prescribe an emotional support raccoon. Bring it to all company zoom meetings without acknowledging it.
Start a rumor in your workplace that you are actually a ghost who died on this floor in 1982.
Yell 'OBJECTION!' at the top of your lungs whenever anyone asks you to take on additional responsibilities.
Eat an entire raw onion in the shower while playing medieval war chants to intimidate your self-doubt.
Flee the country under the alias 'Doctor Linguine' and start an artisanal goat cheese sanctuary.
Send a certified glitter bomb to your inner child to teach them that life is chaotic and sparkling.
Respond to every urgent text message with an uncaptioned stock photo of a perplexed pelican.
Challenge your anxiety to a formal sunrise duel with foam swords behind your neighborhood supermarket.
Wear a velvet wizard cloak to family dinners and only speak in cryptic rhyming prophecies.
Legally change your first name to 'Page Not Found' so government paperwork bounces automatically.
Stick googly eyes on all your credit cards so they glare at you in silent disappointment during impulsive checkouts.
Whenever someone gives you constructive criticism, whisper 'The ancient texts foretold this' and toss a smoke bomb.
Hire a four-piece brass band to follow you around and play a sad trombone sound whenever you drop your keys.
Cut all human contact and make all important life and financial decisions using a Magic 8-Ball.
Host a candlelit memorial service in your backyard for your abandoned hobby supplies.
Take a vow of absolute silence, broken exclusively when ordering spicy chicken nuggets at 2:00 AM.
Wear swimming goggles and flippers to your next job interview to display bold aquatic adaptability.
Scream directly into a jar of peanut butter, seal it tightly, and bury it under an oak tree.
Declare your living room an autonomous pirate republic and demand customs declaration forms from visiting guests.
Adopt a feral pigeon, name him your Senior VP of Operations, and consult him before sending difficult emails.
Carry around a clipboard and a yellow safety vest at all times; you can walk into any restricted area unquestioned.
Whenever someone tells you their horoscope sign, nod intensely and say 'That explains the smell'.
Rebrand your social awkwardness as 'high-concept performance art' and charge admission to your conversations.
Drink warm chocolate milk out of a hollowed-out bell pepper to awaken dormant neural pathways.
Set your alarm clock to the Soviet national anthem played on a recorder with incorrect fingerings.
Throw a housewarming party for the pile of clothes on your bedroom chair that has attained sentience.
Tell everyone you are a secret agent whose cover story is being extraordinarily average and unremarkable.
Stare unblinkingly at the nearest wall whenever small talk starts until the other person slowly backs away.
Replace all family photos in your house with portraits of actor Nicolas Cage eating cake.
Sign all official documents with a stamp that reads 'CERTIFIED PURE CHAOS'.
Write your deepest secrets on helium balloons, release them into the sky, and make them God's problem.
Whenever you make a mistake, look up into an imaginary camera like you're on a 2000s mockumentary sitcom.
Wear two different shoes every day to establish yourself as an enigmatic visionary who operates beyond footwear dogma.
Order a pizza to your neighbor's house, then knock on their door and ask if they want to split it.
Tell your boss that your psychic advisor strictly forbade you from doing PowerPoint presentations this quarter.
Communicate exclusively through interpretive dance when explaining technical software bugs.
Fill your pockets with dry cereal so you can dramatically toss a handful like confetti in triumphant moments.
Write a 5-star review for yourself on Google Maps under the category 'Historical Landmark'.
Bring a miniature potted cactus to dinner dates and introduce it as your chaperone and moral compass.
Lie flat on the floor in public spaces for 3 minutes to reset your spiritual equilibrium and puzzle bystanders.
